prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Sentinel Vale: EO mission ground segment (plan, acquire, operate, produce, archive, access control; excludes spacecraft, launch, user processing); security: least privilege, strong auth, segmentation, audit. Mission Control Center (Bluebell): real-time ops, anomaly response, releases validated commands, owns contact schedule/routing policy; time-limited elevated access with approved shift role; declares continuity modes (objective, duration, exit criteria); sends constraints to Mission Planning System (MPS), receives command preparation package; demonstrates continuous console coverage, complete handover logs. MPS uses Laser Retroreflector Window; applies Ephemeris Delta Note in schedule validation. Spacecraft Operations Team (SOT): console lead declares pass status, authorizes commands, pauses on telemetry mismatch; uses Antenna Deicing Notice, Pass Replay Packet; receives maneuver recommendation package; day-in-the-life rehearsal. Escalation console>discipline lead>mission management. Stack queued only with MCC+SOT concurrence. Command Validation Gateway (Osprey): shall validate stacks, reject unapproved edits/missing provenance/expired config/out-of-window/missing authorization, validation result, operator acknowledgment; accepts Star Tracker Mask File from Flight Dynamics Facility (Mistral) only if matching security baseline; consults Telemetry Ingest Service, Orbit Determination Engine. Mistral sends ephemerides to MCC, MPS, PPF. Cybersecurity Desk: receives Security Exception Ticket from Ground Network Manager (Juniper); validates alert routing, privileged access, incident coordination. Juniper coordinates cross-site failover; accepts antenna baseline only with current maintenance clearances for North S-Band, South S-Band, Kiruna X-Band, Svalbard X-Band Antennas. Network Control System (Lantern): enforces routing, sends MCC antenna status, link config; records outage rehearsals. Flight Dynamics Team: Doppler Residual Report, Ephemeris Delta Note; degraded-data rehearsal. Payload Calibration Team: Calibration Patch Bundle. Product Quality Service: Product Hold List to User Services Portal (blocks release until cleared; no speculative cause before incident lead approval). Payload Processing Facility (Forgehouse): quarantine unproven lineage; Primary Processing Cluster pauses nonessential queues; Backup Processing Cluster transfer after custody/baseline/authorization verified, uses Storage Watermark Snapshot for capacity. Long Term Archive (Granite): custody reference, Storage Watermark Snapshot; reconcile delayed ingest; retrieval tests before stable. Cedar suspends schedule publication on anomaly. Document units:
S244: Operational key performance indicators include contact success rate, telemetry completeness, command validation timeliness, product latency, product quality disposition time, archive availability, help desk responsiveness, and unresolved anomaly age.
S245: Each key performance indicator has an assigned data source, sampling interval, review owner, threshold, and corrective action trigger so that routine reporting does not depend on informal judgment.
S246: The primary monthly service review compares actual performance against the accepted baseline and records trend explanations for any measure that moves outside the watch band.
S247: The Primary Processing Cluster and Backup Processing Cluster are baselined with approved software versions, processing configurations, capacity reservations, monitoring checks, and rollback instructions before handover.
S248: Configuration baselines for ground software, operational procedures, interface control data, account roles, and monitoring rules are frozen at readiness review entry and changed only through approved change control.
S249: Handover to routine mission service is authorized when acceptance evidence is complete, rehearsals meet their objectives, open risks are acknowledged by accountable owners, and support teams confirm on-call coverage.
S250: After handover, the first operational reporting cycle is treated as a stabilization period in which deviations are reviewed daily and permanent process changes are deferred until sufficient evidence is available.
